page: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v7 is a compute-focused yet high-memory virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, with single-threaded core execution. The CPU configuration provides 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, which significantly exceeds conventional compute-optimized memory allocations. No bundled local storage is included, requiring users to rely on external network-attached Premium Storage volumes. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and operates without discrete hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluation reveals exceptional single-threaded performance. The instance registers top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests (3,727.59) and Geekbench 6 single-core (2,842.0) and multi-core (20,878.0) benchmarks. High execution efficiency is evident in compression workloads, recording 41.09 GB/sec in gzip compression and 17.45 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Small-scale language model inference exhibits strong throughput, delivering 446.22 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng, static web serving (32.45 GB/sec), and Redis SET operations (46.62 million ops/sec) align within average percentiles.

Given its elevated single-core frequency and sizable memory footprint, the F16ams_v7 provides strong resource density for compute workloads with expanded working memory sets. Primary fit includes batch data transformations, compilation tasks, image and text processing pipelines, and in-memory analytics that do not depend on local NVMe disk arrays.
